compatibility.title: Which Alfa Romeo Models Use the 955A9000?
compatibility.intro: The 955A9000 was the flagship diesel engine for Alfa Romeo's 159, Brera and Spider range from 2005 to 2011. It's a 2.4‑litre five‑cylinder engine that delivers substantial torque and was praised for its distinctive sound and performance. In 2010, it was joined (and partially replaced) by the 2.0 JTDm 170 hp in some markets.

costGuide.title: Alfa Romeo 955A9000 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 955A9000 typically takes 12-14 hours at £65-£75/hr (independent Alfa Romeo specialist) - main dealer rates are significantly higher. The five‑cylinder engine is slightly more complex to work on than the four‑cylinder JTDm units.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the DPF system (the five‑cylinder is particularly sensitive to DPF issues), the condition of the injectors, and the timing belt service history - this is an interference engine. A used unit with documented belt replacement and DPF history will command a premium. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Alfa Romeo 955A9000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: DPF and EGR System Clogging - a significant issue on 2.4 JTDm
items.whatHappens: The 2.4 JTDm's DPF and EGR system is a known weak point, particularly on cars used for short journeys. The DPF is expensive to replace, and EGR valve issues can cause performance and economy problems. The 2.4 JTDm is more sensitive to DPF issues than the 1.9 JTDm due to its larger displacement and higher fuel throughput.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning or replacement (£800-£1,800) and EGR cleaning or replacement (£300-£600) can resolve the issue. Regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration is essential. If the DPF is clogged beyond cleaning, replacement can be a significant cost. Read our full DPF and EGR guide

items.title: Fuel Injector Failure - rough running and starting issues
items.whatHappens: The 2.4 JTDm's common‑rail injectors can fail, with symptoms including rough idle, misfires, excessive smoke, poor fuel economy, and hard starting. Injector failure can lead to bore wash and cylinder damage if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector replacement (£300-£600 per injector) can resolve the issue if caught early. If injector failure causes bore wash, the engine typically requires full replacement. Read our full injector failure guide

items.title: Timing Belt Failure - snapped belt and bent valves
items.whatHappens: The 2.4 JTDm uses a timing belt, not a chain. Failure to replace the belt at the recommended interval (every 5 years or 60,000-100,000 miles) can result in a snapped belt. The engine is an interference design - pistons hit valves, bending them and requiring extensive cylinder head work or full engine replacement.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing belt replacement is essential preventative maintenance (£500-£900). If the belt snaps while driving, the engine is typically destroyed - full replacement is the only option. Read our full timing belt failure guide

items.title: Dual Mass Flywheel (DMF) Wear - rattle and clutch judder
items.whatHappens: The 2.4 JTDm produces substantial torque (400 Nm), which puts significant stress on the dual mass flywheel (DMF). Symptoms include a rattling noise on startup or at idle, clutch judder, and vibration through the pedal.
items.repairVsReplace: DMF replacement is a significant job (£500-£1,200) and should be undertaken when the clutch is being replaced.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 955A9000
variants.intro: The 955A9000 is part of Fiat's JTDm diesel family. It is commonly confused with: | Similar Code | What It Is | Link | |---|---|---| | 939A2000 | 2.4 JTDm in the Alfa Romeo 159 (2005-2007) - 200 hp, same architecture as 955A9000 but early ECU calibration | Alfa Romeo 939A2000 engine | | 939A3000 | 2.4 JTDm Q4 (four‑wheel drive) variant - 200 hp, different ECU and emissions hardware | Alfa Romeo 939A3000 engine | | 841B0000 | 2.4 JTD in Lancia Thesis - older pre‑common‑rail version, less refined | Lancia 841B0000 engine | | 844A0000 | 2.4 JTDm in Fiat Croma - similar architecture but different ECU and emissions calibration | Fiat 844A0000 engine | How to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block (typically on the front or side of the engine) and appears on the V5C registration document and in the vehicle's VIN. If you're unsure, enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact fitment. Why the difference matters: The 955A9000 is the 210 hp variant, while the 939A2000 is the 200 hp variant with a different ECU calibration. Fitting the wrong variant can cause ECU incompatibility, DPF system differences, and emissions test failures. The Q4 variant (939A3000) has additional emissions hardware for the 4WD system.

relatives.description: - the older 2.4‑litre diesel (pre‑common‑rail, 2000-2005) that the 955A9000 replaced; it produced 150-175 hp and lacked the common‑rail injection system of the JTDm. It's less refined and less powerful but simpler and with fewer DPF issues.

- the 200 hp variant of the 2.4 JTDm fitted to early 159, Brera and Spider (2005-2007); it uses the same architecture as the 955A9000 but with different ECU calibration for Euro 4 emissions compliance.
- the 200 hp Q4 (four‑wheel drive) variant of the 2.4 JTDm; it has additional emissions hardware for the 4WD system and a different ECU calibration. If your car is a Q4, this is the engine you need.

- the smaller 2.0‑litre diesel that partially replaced the 2.4 JTDm in the 159 and Brera from 2010 onward; it produces 170 hp and is more fuel‑efficient but lacks the 2.4's torque and five‑cylinder character.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 955A9000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 2.4 JTDm can seem tempting at £1,200-£2,200, but carries significant risk. You don't know the condition of the DPF, EGR valve, injectors, timing belt, or dual mass flywheel - all of which can fail on higher‑mileage units. The DPF is particularly expensive to replace on the 2.4 JTDm. If you must buy used, insist on documented proof of timing belt replacement, DPF service history, and regular oil changes using the correct 5W‑30 low‑SAPS oil.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** For most 955A9000 replacements, a professionally reconditioned unit is the right call. A proper recon addresses the engine's known weak points: the timing belt and tensioner are replaced, injectors are tested or replaced, the DPF and EGR are cleaned or replaced, the water pump is replaced, and all gaskets and seals are renewed. With a 12‑24 month warranty, this is the lowest‑risk option for a £2,500-£5,000+ investment.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for this engine only when the original block is in good condition and the vehicle has significant collector value - e.g., a low‑mileage Brera or Spider. A rebuild allows for upgraded internals and improved DPF management, but for most owners, a reconditioned exchange unit offers better value and less downtime. Expect £4,000-£6,500+ for a full rebuild.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All reconditioned and rebuilt 955A9000 units can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Alfa Romeo specialists, with nationwide delivery and a minimum 12‑month warranty on every installation. **VEHICLE VALUE NOTE (mandatory):** The 955A9000 sits in vehicles ranging from £3,000-£7,000 (higher‑mileage 159, Brera) to £10,000-£20,000+ (low‑mileage, well‑specified examples, particularly the Brera S and Spider). A reconditioned unit at £2,500-£5,000+ represents 15-40% of the vehicle's value on most hosts - approaching the threshold where replacement may not be financially sensible on older examples. On a sub‑£4,000 example, evaluate the overall vehicle condition and service history before committing; a used unit with documented service history may be the more pragmatic choice, or consider whether the repair is economically justified at all.

items.question: How much does an Alfa Romeo 955A9000 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned 955A9000 costs £2,500-£5,000+ supply‑only, plus £780-£1,050 for fitting at a specialist Alfa Romeo workshop. Used units start from £1,200, and full rebuilds range from £4,000-£6,500+. Prices vary significantly by whether the timing belt, injectors, DPF, and EGR have been replaced. The 210 hp variant commands a premium over the 200 hp version. A used engine without documented timing belt and DPF history is a gamble - avoid it.

items.question: What are the common problems with the 955A9000?
items.answer: The most significant issues are DPF and EGR clogging (the 2.4 JTDm is particularly sensitive), fuel injector failure, timing belt failure (if maintenance is neglected), and dual mass flywheel (DMF) wear. The DPF system on the 2.4 is expensive to replace and is a major weak point on UK cars. Regular motorway driving is essential for DPF regeneration. Timing belt replacement every 5 years or 60,000-100,000 miles is critical.

items.answer: The 955A9000 is fitted to the Alfa Romeo 159 (2005-2011), Brera (2005-2010), and Spider (2006-2011) in 200 hp and 210 hp outputs. It was the flagship diesel for the 939 platform and is renowned for its distinctive five‑cylinder sound and substantial torque delivery. The 210 hp version is the most sought‑after variant. items.answer: For most owners, a reconditioned unit offers the best balance - it includes new timing belt, injectors (tested/replaced), DPF and EGR cleaned/replaced, and a 12‑24 month warranty. Used units are cheaper but carry risk of DPF and injector issues; full rebuilds are justified only for high‑value or collector cars. Reconditioned from £2,500; used from £1,200; rebuilt from £4,000. A used engine without documented DPF service history is a significant risk.

items.question: How do I tell the 955A9000 apart from the 939A2000 and 939A3000?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block (typically on the front or side of the engine), and appears on the V5C and in the VIN. The 955A9000 is the 210 hp variant (2007-2011). The 939A2000 is the 200 hp variant (2005-2007); the 939A3000 is the 200 hp Q4 (four‑wheel drive) variant. All share the same 2.4 JTDm architecture but have different ECU and emissions hardware. Fitting the wrong variant can cause ECU and emissions compatibility issues.
bullets: All share the same 2.4 JTDm architecture but have different ECU and emissions hardware.
Fitting the wrong variant can cause ECU and emissions compatibility issues.

items.question: How reliable is the 955A9000 compared to the older 2.4 JTD?
items.answer: The 955A9000 is significantly more refined and powerful than the older 2.4 JTD, with common‑rail injection delivering smoother power and better fuel economy. However, the modern emissions systems (DPF, EGR) introduce additional failure points that the simpler 2.4 JTD doesn't have. The older engine is more robust but less powerful, less economical, and noisier. Regular servicing and using the correct 5W‑30 low‑SAPS oil are critical. Proactive DPF regeneration (motorway driving) is essential on UK cars.
